g: a quienes amo y extraño
a quienes is a relative pronoun for people and is object of both amo and extraño.
e: manténganse así firmes
A reflexive ustedes command: manténganse means ‘stand firm’; así points back to the teaching just given.

g: que se pongan de acuerdo
rogar que takes subjunctive; se pongan is the plural reflexive form because two women are addressed.
e: en el Señor
en el Señor locates the requested agreement within their shared relationship to the Lord.

g: te pido que ayudes
te is an object pronoun addressing one person; que ayudes is subjunctive after pedir.
e: el libro de la vida
A traditional biblical image of a register of names; libro de means ‘book of’.

g: Alégrense siempre
Alégrense is an affirmative ustedes command of alegrarse; siempre modifies the command, ‘always’.
e: en el Señor
The repeated phrase specifies the sphere of rejoicing: ‘in the Lord’.

g: Que su amabilidad sea evidente
Que + subjunctive sea expresses an exhortation or wish: ‘Let your gentleness be evident’.
e: El Señor está cerca
estar cerca means ‘be near’; the concise statement gives the reason for the preceding appeal.

g: No se inquieten por nada
Negative ustedes commands use subjunctive inquieten; por nada means ‘about nothing’.
e: con oración y ruego
con introduces the means used when presenting requests; the nouns are joined by y.

g: que sobrepasa todo entendimiento
que begins a relative clause describing la paz de Dios; sobrepasa is singular for paz.
e: cuidará sus corazones y sus pensamientos
The future cuidará promises guarding both coordinated nouns, hearts and thoughts.

g: todo lo que sea excelente
lo que creates a neuter ‘whatever’ clause; sea is subjunctive after the indefinite todo.
e: consideren bien
The affirmative ustedes command consideren is modified by bien: ‘consider carefully’.

g: lo que de mí han aprendido
lo que means ‘what’; han aprendido is present perfect, and de mí marks the source.
e: el Dios de paz
A genitive phrase: de paz characterizes God as ‘the God of peace’.

g: hayan vuelto a interesarse
hayan vuelto is present perfect subjunctive after de que; volver a + infinitive means ‘begin again’.
e: al fin
An adverbial phrase meaning ‘at last’ or ‘finally’, indicating a delayed renewal.

g: porque esté necesitado
porque here introduces Paul’s denied motive; esté is subjunctive within No digo esto porque.
e: en cualquier situación
cualquier is the shortened form of cualquiera before singular situación: ‘any situation’.

g: He aprendido a vivir
he aprendido is present perfect; a vivir is the infinitive complement naming what was learned.
e: tanto a quedar saciado como a pasar hambre
tanto ... como pairs contrasting infinitive phrases, fullness and hunger.

g: Todo lo puedo
Todo is the fronted direct object; puedo is first-person singular, ‘I can’.
e: en Cristo que me fortalece
que refers to Cristo; me is the object pronoun of fortalece, ‘who strengthens me’.

g: han hecho bien en participar
han hecho bien en + infinitive means ‘have done well in doing’; participar names the action.
e: participar conmigo
participar con means ‘share with’; conmigo combines con + mí.

g: cuando salí de Macedonia
cuando + preterite salí gives the completed time setting, ‘when I left Macedonia’.
e: excepto ustedes
excepto means ‘except’; the readers are singled out from the stated negative.

g: me enviaron ayuda
me is the indirect object before enviaron: ‘they sent help to me’.
e: una y otra vez
An idiom meaning ‘again and again’; it conveys repeated sending.

g: esté tratando de conseguir
esté tratando is a present progressive subjunctive after No digo esto porque; de conseguir completes tratar de.
e: el crédito a su cuenta
A financial metaphor: crédito a su cuenta is ‘credit to your account’.

g: ahora que he recibido
ahora que introduces the current reason; he recibido is present perfect, ‘I have received’.
e: un sacrificio que Dios acepta con agrado
que introduces a clause describing sacrificio; con agrado means ‘with pleasure’.

g: mi Dios les proveerá
les is the indirect object, ‘for you’; proveerá is a future promise.
e: conforme a las gloriosas riquezas
conforme a means ‘according to’ or ‘in keeping with’.

g: sea la gloria
The subjunctive sea makes a doxological wish: ‘may glory be’.
e: por los siglos de los siglos
A fixed biblical idiom meaning ‘forever and ever’.

g: Los hermanos que están conmigo
que están conmigo is a relative clause identifying which brothers send greetings.
e: en Cristo Jesús
This phrase identifies the saints by their relationship ‘in Christ Jesus’.

g: especialmente los de la casa
los de is a noun-like phrase meaning ‘those from’; it omits the repeated santos.
e: la casa del emperador
casa can mean household, not only a physical house; del contracts de + el.

g: Que la gracia ... sea
Que + subjunctive sea forms the closing blessing: ‘May the grace ... be’.
e: con su espíritu
con indicates accompaniment: ‘with your spirit’; su is singular because the addressed community is viewed together.
